hero.lead: A nation of 6.5 million with €1.59 billion earmarked under the EU Growth Plan, the largest envelope in the Western Balkans, and growth of 3.3% projected this year.

capital.heading: The largest envelope in the region, and water for every home.

register.name: Twelve-year green Eurobond
register.detail: Ministry of Finance · traded 28 April 2026 · settled 6 May 2026 · matures 6 May 2038 · coupon 4.875% · yield 5.173% · 200 bp over mid-swaps · issue price 97.384%
register.note: One of three tranches sold together, with €1bn due 2031 to repay bonds due in 2027 and €1.25bn due 2036; demand above €8bn
register.text: A twelve-year green bond of the Republic of Serbia in euros, sold in the first issue Serbia has made in three tranches. Its proceeds go only to green projects; the Ministry names railway improvements and the Belgrade metro, so it is not earmarked to any one of the seven standards.

register.name: Ten-year sustainable bond in US dollars
register.detail: Ministry of Finance · issued 12 June 2024 · coupon 6.00% · swapped into euros at a fixed 4.754% · net proceeds €1.38bn · about 20.3% unallocated in September 2025
register.note: Allocated by September 2025: 25.5% to healthcare, 14.3% to education and 2.5% to water and wastewater
register.text: A ten-year sustainable bond of the Republic of Serbia under its Sustainable Finance Framework of 2024. By September 2025 its proceeds had gone to healthcare, education, socioeconomic advancement, clean transport and water and wastewater, which carry the health, education and water standards.

register.name: Seven-year green Eurobond
register.detail: Ministry of Finance · issued September 2021 · Green Notes due 2028 · coupon 1% · yield 1.26% · more than three times oversubscribed
register.note: The first green bond Serbia issued on international markets; an older instrument, due 2028
register.text: The first green bond of the Republic of Serbia on international markets. By the third quarter of 2022, 28% of the allocated proceeds had gone to sustainable water and wastewater management, which carries the water and shelter standards, and 2% to energy efficiency; none went to renewable energy.

register.name: Inclusive Primary Education Improvement Project
register.detail: World Bank (IBRD) · approved 29 July 2025 · €66.3M ($75M equivalent) · project P181557
register.note: For a quarter of a million primary pupils, among them rural, Roma and disabled children, and at least 20,000 teachers
register.text: A World Bank loan to improve school buildings, especially in disadvantaged areas, and to move primary schools gradually to a whole-day model. It carries the education standard for a quarter of a million primary pupils.

register.name: Second Green Transition Development Policy Loan
register.detail: World Bank · approved 6 March 2025 · €153.7M ($160M equivalent) · second of a series begun in 2023
register.note: Budget support paid against reforms; not earmarked to any one standard
register.text: A World Bank loan to the state budget, paid against reforms that raise the share of renewables in energy production, align environmental law with the EU and tag green and gender spending in the budget. It bears on the energy standard; its funds are not earmarked.

register.name: Policy Coordination Instrument
register.detail: IMF · 36 months, non-financing · approved December 2024 · second review December 2025 · third review concluded June 2026
register.note: No IMF financing; the IMF projects growth of about 2.8% in 2026
register.text: A non-financing IMF programme that anchors Serbia’s fiscal policy and reforms; the 2026 budget keeps the programme’s deficit ceiling of 3% of GDP. It lends nothing, but the IMF states that targeted energy support for vulnerable households should continue, which bears on the energy standard.

register.name: Reform and Growth Facility (EU Growth Plan)
register.detail: European Commission · Reform Agenda approved October 2024 · €111M pre-financing · first tranche of €56.5M approved January 2026 · fourth payment request July 2026
register.note: €167.5 million received by August 2026; €6 billion in all for the Western Balkans: €2 billion in grants, €4 billion in loans
register.text: Grants and concessional loans from the EU, paid against reforms under Serbia’s Reform Agenda: €111 million of pre-financing, then a first tranche of €56.5 million approved in January 2026. Serbia submitted a fourth payment request of more than €108 million in July 2026; its reforms include modernising the electricity grid and strengthening energy security.

register.name: Renovation of health centres (additional loan)
register.detail: Council of Europe Development Bank · approved 16 March 2026 · borrower the Government · additional financing, scope unchanged
register.note: For citizens of Serbia, medical professionals and the surrounding community
register.text: An additional CEB loan to complete planned upgrades and renovations of healthcare facilities across Serbia, covering higher costs on existing sub-projects. It carries the health standard.

register.name: Clinical centres of Belgrade, Novi Sad, Kragujevac and Niš
register.detail: EIB Global · signed 3 November 2025 in Belgrade · backed by an EU guarantee under EFSD+
register.note: Signed with a €35.5 million EU grant for sewerage in Palilula: €192.5 million in all
register.text: An EIB loan to rebuild and extend four major clinical centres, in Belgrade, Novi Sad, Kragujevac and Niš, to strengthen access to quality healthcare. It carries the health standard.

register.name: Sewerage network for Palilula, Belgrade
register.detail: EU grant through the Western Balkans Investment Framework · signed 3 November 2025 · treated wastewater discharged into the Danube
register.note: About 86,000 residents; a project of €85.4 million with an EIB loan and the City of Belgrade, as the minister stated
register.text: An EU grant to build a sewerage network in the Belgrade municipality of Palilula, improving sanitation for around 86,000 residents. It carries the shelter standard, measured by safely managed sanitation, the standard furthest from reach in Serbia.

register.name: Multiannual Operational Programme on Environment and Energy
register.detail: Financing Agreement with the EU · signed 7 August 2025 in Belgrade · €240M in non-repayable EU grants from IPA funds · co-financing rate 26.2%
register.note: Water supply and sewage, wastewater treatment, waste, air quality and energy efficiency in public buildings and households
register.text: An EU programme of €325.2 million, of which €240 million is grants, for public water supply and sewage systems, wastewater treatment and energy efficiency in public buildings and households. It carries the water, shelter and energy standards.

register.name: Clean heating: replacing polluting boiler houses
register.detail: EBRD · signed 12 June 2025 · loan agreement signed by the Minister of Finance · funds passed on by the Ministry of Environmental Protection
register.note: Up to €50 million, for Belgrade, Niš, Valjevo, Zaječar, Novi Pazar and Smederevo
register.text: An EBRD loan to close environmentally harmful boiler houses in six municipalities, with heat pumps, connections to district heating where feasible and energy retrofits of public buildings. It carries the energy standard through cleaner heat and reduces air pollution in Serbian cities.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: Land that can feed the nation and earn abroad, valued and financed against its harvest.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.

items.name: The Diaspora
items.label: Of GDP sent home by citizens abroad, 2025
items.text: Citizens abroad send home a steady share of the economy: a flow that can back long-term finance.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 14.3% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.

items.name: Radanska ruža
items.text: A social enterprise in Lebane, begun by five women with disabilities, single mothers or women who had never worked, that now employs 15 women full time and about 20 more each season making organic ajvar, jams and peppers, and exported 280,000 jars last year.

items.name: Liceulice
items.text: A street magazine published ten times a year by a Belgrade non-profit and sold by more than 180 homeless people, Roma, people with disabilities, users of psychiatric services and older people in Belgrade, Kikinda and Novi Sad, who keep half the earnings from each copy.

items.name: Avlija održivog razvoja
items.text: A social enterprise of Caritas Šabac in Bogatić that runs a restaurant, kitchen, distillery and vegetable greenhouses and sells jams, award-winning rakija and catering; with its sister enterprise it employs 90 people, more than 70% of them people with disabilities.

items.name: Socijalna sinergija
items.text: A social enterprise of Caritas Šabac that sells dry-cleaning, washing, drying and ironing and the upkeep of commercial and residential premises; with its sister enterprise it employs 90 people, more than 70% of them people with disabilities.

items.name: Naša kuća
items.text: A social enterprise in which more than 30 people with developmental disabilities work and earn, and which caters events.

items.name: Zvuci srca
items.text: A café, workshop and shop of the Dečje srce association, run by and employing people with developmental disabilities, alongside a week-long school of life skills and a planned work centre.

items.name: Kafe bar 16
items.text: A café in Belgrade run as a social enterprise within the employment support programme of the Centre for Youth Integration, where young people who grew up in hard circumstances learn, work and earn an income for an independent life.
